extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and patent applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how a U.S. patent application is considered abandoned, examiner procedures for declaring abandonment, and the available petitions, forms, and timing rules for express abandonment, revival, withdrawal from issue, refunds, and publication-avoidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of application abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandoned application is one removed from the Office docket of pending applications through (A) formal abandonment (by the applicant, attorney/agent of record, or registered attorney/agent acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 when filing a continuing application) or (B) failure of applicant to take appropriate action within a specified time at some stage in the prosecution of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References: 37 CFR 1.135 and 1.138. The discussion is concerned with abandonment of the application (not abandonment of the invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express (formal) abandonment — signature and identification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be expressly abandoned by filing a written declaration of abandonment identifying the application in the USPTO. The declaration must be signed by a party authorized under 37 CFR 1.33(b)(1) or (b)(3) (attorney/agent of record), except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A registered attorney or agent not of record who acts under 37 CFR 1.34 when filing a continuing application may expressly abandon the prior application as of the continuing application's filing date. Care must be taken to ensure the abandonment is in accordance with the applicant's desires and that the correct application is identified. If the letter complies with 37 CFR 1.138, the Office should acknowledge receipt (use PTO-1432). A noncompliant letter should receive a fully explanatory letter. A letter received after the statutory period for reply is not acceptable to expressly abandon the application (it is placed in the file but not formally entered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment — filing methods, timing, and acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of express abandonment or petitions under 37 CFR 1.138(c) may be filed electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system or mailed to Mail Stop Express Abandonment; timing is critical for effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When abandonment is claimed to avoid publication, petitions should be received in time for the Pre-Grant Publication Division to act; electronic transmission is recommended when projected publication is less than 3 months away to increase chance of recognition. Action recognizing an express abandonment may take the form of an acknowledgment by the Publishing Division indicating compliance with 37 CFR 1.138. For allowed applications where the issue fee has been paid, an express abandonment must be accompanied by a petition to withdraw an application from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c) (see subsection I. After Payment of Issue Fee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment after payment of the issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If a letter of express abandonment is submitted after payment of the issue fee, the express abandonment must be accompanied by a petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c) and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The express abandonment may not be recognized unless actually received by appropriate officials in time to withdraw the application from issue; the petition must be received and granted before the date of issue. Addressing/transmission options for the petition include mail, facsimile, hand-delivery, or electronic filing; applicants are strongly encouraged to use electronic, facsimile, or hand-carry methods to allow sufficient processing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding publication via express abandonment (37 CFR 1.138(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) to abandon an application to avoid publication will be effective only if recognized and acted on by the Pre-Grant Publication Division in sufficient time to avoid publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, petitions received more than four weeks prior to the projected date of publication have a chance to be effective; it is unlikely a petition filed within four weeks of projected publication will avoid publication. Applicants should expect petitions under 1.138(c) will not be granted unless timely received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of search fee and excess claims fee via express abandonment (37 CFR 1.138(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant seeking a refund of search and excess claims fees by express abandonment must submit a declaration of express abandonment by petition under 37 CFR 1.138(d) before an examination has been made of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on any certificate of mailing/transmission under 37 CFR 1.8 is not considered for determining whether the petition was filed before an examination. If a refund request is not filed with the declaration or within two months after filing the declaration, the Office may retain the entire fees; the two-month period is not extendable. ‘‘Examination has been made’’ is defined by actions shown in the One Patent Service Gateway as having been counted (e.g., first Office action on the merits, restriction/election, notice of allowance, etc.). If PDP status is higher than 031 before/on the day the petition was filed, the petition will be denied. Technical preparations for publication generally begin four months prior to projected publication; timely electronic filing is recommended. Use of form PTO/AIA/24B (or PTO/SB/24B) is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment for failure to reply within statutory period (37 CFR 1.135)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant fails to reply within the time period provided under 37 CFR 1.134 and 1.136, the application will become abandoned unless an Office action indicates otherwise; prosecution to save the application must include a complete and proper reply as required by the condition of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The admission or refusal to admit amendments after final rejection or any amendment not responsive to the last action will not save the application from abandonment. When a reply is a bona fide attempt and substantially complete but inadvertently omits some compliance, applicant may be given a new time period under 1.134 to supply the omission. Examiner must know the dates marking beginning and end of statutory periods in varying situations; see MPEP §§ 512, 513, 710 et seq. Examples of shortened statutory period expiration are in MPEP § 711.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner procedure when amendment filed after statutory period (late amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an amendment is filed after the expiration of the statutory period and is not timely under 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.7, the application is abandoned and remedy is to petition to revive. The examiner should notify applicant using Notice of Abandonment form PTOL-1432 and place the late amendment in the file wrapper but not formally enter it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 7.90 Abandonment, Failure to Reply; 7.98.02 Reply Is Late, Petition To Revive Suggested, Pro Se). A letter of abandonment should not be mailed until after the period for requesting an extension under 37 CFR 1.136(a) has expired. For petitions to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 see MPEP § 711.03(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to revive an abandoned application (37 CFR 1.137) — unintentional delay requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to revive on the grounds that the failure to reply was unintentional must be accompanied by: (1) the required reply; (2) a statement that the entire delay was unintentional; (3) any terminal disclaimer required by 37 CFR 1.137(d); and (4) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No consideration to the substantive petition will be given until the fee is received. The Director may require additional information to determine whether the delay was unintentional. The required items and fees must be submitted promptly under a cover letter entitled 'Petition to Revive.' See methods of correspondence and contact information in MPEP § 711.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficiency of reply (reply not fully responsive) leads to abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An abandonment may result where applicant’s reply is within the period for reply but is not fully responsive to the Office action (insufficiency of reply). A fully responsive reply must be timely filed to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply appears to be a bona fide attempt with inadvertent omission, do not use form paragraph 7.91; instead use form paragraph 7.95. The date on which a petition under 37 CFR 1.136(a) and extension fee have been filed is the date for determining extension period. In no case may an applicant reply outside the six (6) month statutory period or obtain an extension for more than five (5) months beyond the date for reply set forth in an Office action. Examiner should specify why reply is not fully responsive in communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations that may cause abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain procedural situations may result in abandonment even if no simple 'failure to reply' occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: (A) Copying claims from a patent when not suggested by USPTO does not constitute a reply to the last Office action (unless the action relied solely on that patent); (B) abandonment via withdrawal of or failure to prosecute an appeal to the PTAB; (C) abandonment via dismissal of appellate or civil action without filing an amendment putting application in condition for issue; (D) issues where claims are suggested for interference near end of reply period; (E) filing a CPA under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (considered express abandonment in some situations); (F) continued prosecution application (RCE) improperly filed without appropriate fee or submission where filing is treated as withdrawal of appeal; (G) filing an improper RCE when reply to a final action is outstanding may cause abandonment; (H) improper RCE prior to payment of issue fee may cause abandonment. See MPEP §§ 706.07(h), 201.06(d), 2300, 1215/1216 as referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings (effect on copendency and dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings are terminated (for purposes such as copendency under 35 U.S.C. 120) in specified situations, with 'before' interpreted as 'not later than' (i.e., 'before' = 'not later than').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situations causing termination include: (A) issue fee not paid and application abandoned for failure to pay the issue fee (proceedings terminated as of the date issue fee was due); (B) application in an interference loses interference to all claims — proceedings terminated as of date appeal was due if no appeal filed; (C) termination after decision by the Board (see MPEP § 1214.06); (D) termination after decision by the court (see MPEP § 1216.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration of a holding of abandonment (insufficiency vs no reply)
rubrics_metrics.description: When advised of abandonment, applicant may ask for reconsideration if they disagree (claiming there was no abandonment in fact); examiner may reverse a holding if an amendment received during the period was in fact responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reversal that the application was never abandoned is not a 'revival' but a determination there was no abandonment. If amendment reached the Office after expiration and there is no dispute as to dates, no reconsideration is possible; where dates or responsiveness are disputed, applicant may take issue and seek correction or petition. See MPEP § 711.03(a)-(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions relating to abandonment — general references and interplay with 37 CFR 1.135/1.137
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135 governs abandonment for failure to reply; 37 CFR 1.137 governs revival of abandoned applications based on unintentional delay (and related rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering petitions (revival, withdraw from issue, set aside holding), refer to the specific CFR provisions. Revival petitions under 1.137 and petitions under 1.313 (withdrawal from issue) have distinct fee and timing requirements and may require additional statements or terminal disclaimers. See MPEP § 711.03(c) for filing and content requirements and MPEP cross-references for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications — citation and prior art use
rubrics_metrics.description: Defensive publication abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications are printed publications and are cited as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) or pre-AIA equivalents effective from Official Gazette publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A defensive publication is a publication (not a patent or application publication) and is prior art as of its publication date; abstracts/abbreviatures are listed under 'Other References' and defensive publications under 'U.S. Patent Documents' in citations. An application or portion thereof used to prepare an abstract/abbreviature may be used as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) effective from actual filing date only for evidence of prior knowledge of another. See MPEP § 711.06 and citation formatting examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms for express abandonment and related petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific forms are recommended/available for filing letters of express abandonment and petitions under subsections of 37 CFR 1.138: PTO/AIA/24 (or PTO/SB/24), PTO/AIA/24A (or PTO/SB/24A), and PTO/AIA/24B (or PTO/SB/24B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/AIA/24 may be used for filing a letter of express abandonment or abandonment in favor of a continuing application. PTO/AIA/24A may be used for a petition for express abandonment under 1.138(c) to avoid publication. PTO/AIA/24B may be used for a petition under 1.138(d) to obtain a refund of search and excess claims fees. Use of recommended forms and electronic filing is encouraged to ensure timely processing.
